issues.legal_issue: A claimant seeking specific performance must establish continuous readiness and willingness to perform the contract, and inconsistent claims that the debt was discharged cannot be reconciled with an unconditional willingness to pay the agreed consideration.
material_facts: The claimant sought specific performance of an agreement to reconvey property but principally asserted that the transaction was a mortgage and that the debt had already been discharged through rent or under debt-relief proceedings.
The claimant sought accounting and offered to pay any amount found due only if the claims of discharge and mortgage redemption were rejected.
In cross-examination, the claimant stated that he had no income, funds, bank account, or source from which to raise the money.
The trial court and the High Court Single Judge found that the claimant was not ready and willing to perform; the High Court Division Bench reversed that finding.
issues.conclusion: The claimant did not prove readiness and willingness to perform the agreement, and was not entitled to specific performance. The Division Bench erred in granting that relief.
issues.legal_principle: Specific Relief Act, 1963, Section 16(c), requires a plaintiff to aver and prove readiness and willingness to perform the essential terms of the contract according to its true construction. The court assesses the plaintiff’s conduct throughout the case and the attending circumstances; a bare pleading or examination-in-chief is insufficient, and the plaintiff must prove that the consideration could be arranged when required. A conditional offer and a claim that the debt was already discharged are inconsistent with an unconditional willingness to pay. The Court relied on N.P. Thirugnanam v. Dr. R. Jagan Mohan Rao, Mahabir Prasad Jain v. Ganga Singh, Pushparani S. Sundaram v. Pauline Manomani James, Manjunath Anandappa v. Tammanasa, Pukhraj D. Jain v. G. Gopalakrishna, and Prem Raj v. D.L.F. Housing & Construction Pvt. Ltd.

rule.if: specific_performance_suit and (claimant_asserts_debt_already_discharged or claimant_makes_only_conditional_offer) and claimant_lacks_evidence_of_ability_to_pay

predicates.specific_performance_suit: A claimant brought a suit seeking an order that the other party carry out an agreement.
predicates.claimant_asserts_debt_already_discharged: The claimant asserted that the obligation to pay had already ended, including by repayment, set-off, or discharge.
predicates.claimant_makes_only_conditional_offer: The claimant offered to pay only if the claimant’s other claims were rejected or an accounting showed an amount remained due.
predicates.claimant_lacks_evidence_of_ability_to_pa: The claimant provided no evidence that the required money was available or could be arranged when payment was required.

issues.definition: When a claimant seeking performance asserts that the debt is discharged or offers to pay only conditionally, and provides no evidence of an ability to pay, the claimant is not entitled to specific performance.

issues.legal_issue: A sale accompanied by a separate agreement to reconvey is not a mortgage by conditional sale when the reconveyance condition is not included in the document that effects or purports to effect the sale.
material_facts: The parties executed a deed of sale and a separate agreement to reconvey the property on the same day.
The reconveyance condition was contained in the separate agreement rather than in the deed of sale.
The claimant nevertheless asserted that the transaction was a mortgage securing a loan.
issues.conclusion: The transaction was a sale with a condition of repurchase, not a mortgage by conditional sale.
issues.legal_principle: Transfer of Property Act, 1882, Section 58(c), provides that a transaction is not a mortgage by conditional sale where the condition for transfer back is not embodied in the document that effects or purports to effect the sale. A mortgage leaves a debt and a right to redeem; a sale with a condition of repurchase does not create a debt and gives only a personal right enforceable according to the agreement. The Court relied on Pandit Chunchun Jha v. Sheikh Ebadat Ali, Shri Bhaskar Waman Joshi v. Shri Narayan Rambilas Agarwal, K. Simrathmull v. Nanjalingiah Gowder, Mushir Mohammed Khan v. Sajeda Bano, and Tamboli Ramanlal Motilal v. Ghanchi Chimanlal Keshavlal.

predicates.sale_with_repurchase_arrangement: The parties completed a transfer of property and agreed that the transferor could later obtain a transfer back.
predicates.reconveyance_condition_in_separate_docum: The condition for transferring the property back appeared in a document separate from the document effecting the sale.

issues.definition: When a property transfer includes a repurchase arrangement but the reconveyance condition is in a separate document, the transaction is a sale rather than a mortgage by conditional sale.

issues.legal_issue: A Division Bench hearing an intra-court appeal should ordinarily avoid disturbing concurrent factual findings without cogent reasons.
material_facts: The trial court found that the claimant was not ready and willing to perform the agreement and that the property was not undervalued.
The High Court Single Judge affirmed the trial court’s findings.
The Division Bench reversed those findings, and the Supreme Court found that it had failed to consider material pleadings and testimony properly.
issues.conclusion: The Division Bench should not have displaced the concurrent findings without cogent reasons, and its judgment could not stand.
issues.legal_principle: An intra-court appeal is not confined to the limits of Section 100 of the Code of Civil Procedure, but its entertainment is discretionary; ordinarily, a Division Bench should not differ from a Single Judge’s factual findings without cogent reasons. An appellate court should also exercise restraint when findings depend on the evidence. The Court relied on Smt. Asha Devi v. Dukhi Sao, Collector of Customs, Bombay v. Swastic Woollens (P) Ltd., West Bengal Electricity Regulatory Commission v. CESC Ltd., Commissioner of Customs, Chennai v. Adani Exports Ltd., and Manjunath Anandappa v. Tammanasa.

predicates.intra_court_appeal: A party appealed within the same court system from a judgment of a single judge to a division bench.
predicates.concurrent_factual_findings: The trial court and the single judge reached the same factual findings.
predicates.no_cogent_reason_for_departure: The appellate court departed from those findings without a cogent reason for doing so.

issues.definition: In an intra-court appeal, when the trial court and single judge agree on factual findings and there is no cogent reason to depart, the appellate court should ordinarily preserve those findings.

issues.legal_issue: A long interval before repayment and the absence of interest, without more, do not establish that a property was undervalued or warrant exercising discretion to grant specific performance.
material_facts: The trial court and the High Court Single Judge found that the property was not undervalued and that the stated consideration was not inadequate.
The Division Bench relied on the agreement allowing payment after a period of years without interest as a circumstance supporting the claimant’s case and the exercise of discretion in his favour.
issues.conclusion: The Division Bench committed a manifest error by treating the delayed repayment without interest as a sufficient circumstance to support its conclusion on undervaluation and discretionary relief.
issues.legal_principle: Specific performance is discretionary under Section 20 of the Specific Relief Act, 1963, and is not granted merely because it is lawful to do so. The existence of a circumstance that makes relief unavailable under Section 20(2) may remove the question of discretion; otherwise, discretion must be exercised on relevant grounds. The Court relied on Sargunam v. Chidambram, Mademsetty Satyanarayana v. G. Yelloji Rao, and M.V. Shankar Bhat v. Claude Pinto.

predicates.specific_performance_proceeding: A party sought a court order requiring performance of an agreement.
predicates.lower_courts_found_no_undervaluation: The trial court and the reviewing single judge found that the property was not undervalued.
predicates.delayed_repayment_without_interest_is_th: The appellate court relied only on the long repayment interval and absence of interest to support undervaluation or favourable discretionary relief.

issues.definition: In a specific performance proceeding, a finding against the lower courts’ conclusion on undervaluation or in favour of discretionary relief cannot rest only on delayed repayment without interest.
